title: आधारभूत तहमा शिक्षकको पेसागत मनोबल विकासको अवस्था {The State of Teachers' Professional Morale Development at the Basic Level}
nepali: प्रस्तुत अध्ययन आधारभूत तहमा शिक्षकको पेसागत मनोबल विकासको अवस्था पहिचान पर्ने उद्देश्यले गरिएको हो । यो अध्ययन कीर्तिपुरस्थित दुई वटा सामुदायिक माध्यमिक विद्यालयको आधारभूत तहमा अध्यापन गर्ने शिक्षकहरू तथा प्रधानाध्यापकमा केन्द्रित रहेको छ । यस अध्ययनमा अध्ययनकर्ता आफैँ विद्यालयमा गई गहन अन्तर्वार्ताका माध्यमबाट सूचनाहरू सङ्कलन गरी प्राप्त सूचनाहरूलाई व्याख्यात्मक र वर्णनात्मक विधिद्वारा विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यस अध्ययनमा शिक्षकको पेसागत मनोबल विकासका कार्यक्रमहरू शिक्षकको विषयगत आवश्यकता र मागमा आधारित नभएको पाइयो । तालिम बढुवा प्रयोजन र औपचारिकतामा मात्र सीमित रहेको देखियो । शिक्षक स्वयम्ले आफ्नो प्रयास र स्वअध्ययनबाट पेसागत विकास गर्न सक्ने तथ्य प्राप्त भएको छ । साथै शिक्षकको पेसागत मनोबल विकासमा स्थानीय निकायको भूमिका प्रभावकारी हुन नसकेको, विद्यालयमा नियमित कक्षा अवलोकन र सुपेरीवेक्षण हुन नसकेको, कार्यमूलक अनुसन्धान तथा लेखरचना प्रकाशन गर्ने कार्यमा संस्थागत प्रयास हुन नसकेको र केही शिक्षकहरू पेसागत विकासका अवसरबाट समेत वञ्चित भएको पाइयो । शिक्षा मन्त्रालयले शिक्षण पेसामा प्रवेश गरेदेखि नै शिक्षकहरूलाई पेसागत मनोबल विकासका अवसर प्राप्त हुने नीति तर्जुमा गर्नाका साथै विद्यालय तथा स्थानीय निकायले विद्यार्थीको नतिजा उत्कृष्ट गर्न सफल हुने शिक्षकलाई उचित पुरस्कारको व्यवस्था गर्नुपर्ने तथा स्थानीय आवश्यकतामा आधारित तालिमको व्यवस्थापन गरी पेसागत मनोबल बढाउनु पर्ने देखिन्छ । {The present study has been undertaken to explore the state of professional morale development of the teachers teaching at the basic level. It has been confined to the teachers and head teachers teaching in two different community secondary schools located in Kirtipur. In this study, the researcher himself visited the schools, and conducted an indepth interview for the purpose of data collection. The collected data have been analyzed and interpreted following the descriptive-and-explanatory method. The results from the analysis depicted that the activities and programs proposed for the professional morale development of the teachers were not based on the subject specific needs and demands of the teachers. The training was seen just as a formality and only for the purpose of promotion. However, the teachers have made their own attempts to develop their professional morale by means of self-studies and initiations. The teachers reported that the role of local agencies has not been instrumentalized for the professional morale development of the teachers. Neither there is a provision of regular monitoring and supervision nor the institutional effort has been made for action research and teachers’ publications. A few teachers have been found to be deprived of the opportunities of their professional development. The findings of the study imply that the Ministry of Education should devise the policy of professional morale development of the teachers when they get entry into the teaching profession. The local government and the school stakeholders should provide rewards and/or incentives for the teachers who performed well to enhance students’ achievement. There is a need for managing training programs to the teachers considering the existing local need and the essence in order to develop their professional morale.}
american_english: The present study was undertaken with the objective of identifying the state of teachers' professional morale development at the basic level. This study is focused on the teachers and head teachers who teach at the basic level in two community secondary schools located in Kirtipur. In this study, the researcher himself visited the schools, collected information through in-depth interviews, and analyzed the obtained information using explanatory and descriptive methods. In this study, the programs for teachers' professional morale development were found not to be based on the teachers' subject-specific needs and demands. Training was found to be limited to promotion purposes and mere formality. The fact that teachers can achieve professional development through their own efforts and self-study has been established. Furthermore, the role of local bodies in teachers' professional morale development was not found effective; regular classroom observation and supervision did not take place in schools; institutional effort in action research and the work of writing and publishing was not found; and some teachers were found to be deprived of opportunities for professional development. It is seen that the Ministry of Education should formulate a policy ensuring that teachers receive opportunities for professional morale development from the very moment they enter the teaching profession, and that schools and local bodies should set up appropriate rewards for teachers who succeed in improving student outcomes, and manage training based on local needs in order to boost professional morale.

It is seen that the Ministry of Education should formulate a policy to ensure that teachers receive opportunities for professional morale development from the moment they enter the teaching profession, and that schools and local bodies should put in place appropriate rewards for teachers who succeed in improving student outcomes, and manage training based on local needs so as to raise professional morale.
australian_english: The present study was carried out with a view to identifying the state of teachers' professional morale development at the basic level. This study is focused on the teachers and head teachers teaching at the basic level in two community secondary schools in Kirtipur. In this study, the researcher himself went into the schools, gathered information through in-depth interviews, and analysed the obtained information by explanatory and descriptive methods. In this study, the programmes for teachers' professional morale development turned out not to be based on the teachers' subject-specific needs and demands. Training was found to be limited to promotion purposes and mere formality. The fact that teachers can achieve professional development through their own efforts and self-study has come to light. What's more, the role of local bodies in teachers' professional morale development was not found effective; regular classroom observation and supervision did not take place in schools; institutional effort in action research and writing and publishing was not found; and some teachers were found to be deprived of opportunities for professional development. It's clear the Ministry of Education should draw up a policy to make sure teachers get opportunities for professional morale development right from the time they start in the teaching profession, and that schools and local bodies should set up proper rewards for teachers who manage to lift student outcomes, and run training based on local needs to boost professional morale.
informal_english: This study set out to figure out where teachers' professional morale development stands at the basic level. It looked at the teachers and head teachers teaching at the basic level in two community secondary schools in Kirtipur. The researcher himself went into the schools and gathered the info through in-depth interviews, then analysed what he got using explanatory and descriptive methods. Turns out the programmes meant to boost teachers' professional morale weren't based on what teachers actually needed or asked for subject-wise. Training was pretty much limited to promotion and going through the motions. The study also found that teachers can develop professionally through their own effort and self-study. On top of that, local bodies didn't pull their weight when it came to teachers' professional morale development; regular classroom observation and supervision just didn't happen; there was no institutional push around action research and writing and publishing; and some teachers missed out on professional development opportunities altogether. The Ministry of Education needs to put a policy in place so teachers get professional morale development opportunities from the get-go of their teaching career. Schools and local bodies should reward teachers who manage to lift student results, and run training based on what the locals actually need, to give professional morale a proper boost.
